title: Beldesk Week 3 — the journey of one question

slides.title: Beldesk — Week 3
slides.label: Opening
slides.speaker: Efe
slides.notes: Hello, we are Beldesk, a Turkish and English assistant for the fictional Yeşilvadi Municipality. Today you follow one real citizen question through our new retrieval pipeline.

slides.title: Eight deliverables and where each one stands
slides.label: Week 3 / W3.1–W3.8
slides.speaker: Efe
slides.notes: Eight requirements this week. 7 are done; W3.4 is partial, as its card explains. Each status comes from our data file.

slides.title: One question enters; staff-only text never competes
slides.label: W3.1 / W3.2 · access gate
slides.speaker: Efe
slides.notes: Here is the question: a tenant asks what to prepare for a water subscription and does not know the old subscriber number. Before any ranking, an access gate removes the staff-only document, YV-D031. Its 2 chunks never compete, so 90 of 92 section chunks remain for a public question.

slides.title: Two searches rank the same chunks differently
slides.label: W3.3 · two lanes
slides.speaker: Efe
slides.notes: The question now splits into two lanes. BM25 ranks chunks by shared words; the multilingual embedding model ranks them by meaning. Both put YV-D003#requirements first, but the rest of the lists differ. The lines connect the 3 chunks both lanes found in their top five.

slides.title: RRF merges the lists; the reranker reads each passage
slides.label: W3.3 · fuse and rerank
slides.speaker: Efe
slides.notes: Reciprocal rank fusion merges the two lists using only their ranks, so one constant k equal to 60 replaces score calibration. Then a cross-encoder reranker reads the question together with each passage. YV-D003#procedure jumps from 11 to 3. Only the top five reach the model.

slides.title: The recorded answer points to the sentence it used
slides.label: W3.4 · recorded demo
slides.speaker: Efe
slides.notes: This is a recorded run, not a live call: Recorded citizen-v2 Gemini 3.1 response / 24 Nov 2026. The answer arrives claim by claim. Every claim carries a citation number, and each citation draws a line to the exact sentence it quotes. Our validator checks that each quote occurs in the cited source; the judge then rated 3 of 3 claims supported. The English lines are our translation.

slides.title: No authorized evidence: no model call, one fixed sentence
slides.label: W3.4 · fixed fallback
slides.speaker: Efe
slides.notes: When no authorized passage is left, the shelf is empty and the code never calls the model. It returns one fixed sentence; this part is a deterministic software check. In the recorded model run, null of 6 unavailable-information controls got that fallback; W3-U004 was answered instead.

slides.title: Evidence in the top five for 32 / 32 questions
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3.5
slides.speaker: Doruk
slides.notes: I am Doruk, with the measurements. Each dot is one of 32 answerable questions, sixteen Turkish and sixteen English, and its number is the rank of the first registered evidence. At rank one, 19 light up; by rank three, 30; by rank five, 32. The whiskers are Wilson intervals: even a perfect score only bounds hit at five above 0.89. The 6 unanswerable controls are excluded. One ring matters: all required facets reach the top five for 31 / 32. MRR at ten is 0.759.

slides.title: Two ablations, one switch at a time
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3.7
slides.speaker: Doruk
slides.notes: We changed one component at a time on the same 32 questions. Switching the reranker off drops hit at five from 1.000 to 0.906 and MRR from 0.759 to 0.689: 3 questions gained evidence with the reranker and 0 lost it; the exact test gives p = 0.25. Switching candidates from hybrid to dense gives MRR 0.761 against 0.759. With 32 questions, none of these differences is significant.

slides.title: 89 of 90 claims match their cited source
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3.6
slides.speaker: Doruk
slides.notes: Faithfulness has an explicit denominator. Of 38 cases, 36 produced valid answers and 35 were judged, giving 90 claims. 1 is unsupported, from W3-R017. An audit corrected the definition: a validated fixed refusal contributes no claims, so 2 of 91 became 1 of 90. This is a provisional automatic judge.

slides.title: 9 rows measured; the rest stay null
slides.label: Scoreboard / W3
slides.speaker: Doruk
slides.notes: The same thirteen rows as Week two, in the same order, now with n and intervals. Test set size is 38. End-to-end accuracy stays null: we have no answer-adequacy rubric yet. Abstention is 0.833 on only 6 controls, so its interval is wide. Unsupported claims are 0.011 on 90 claims. Hit at five and MRR are new this week. The rows task success, pass k, injection success stay null this week. Latency is 4.7 seconds without waits. Cost per task is a list-price estimate of 0.00104 dollars, not a bill; actual spend is 0 dollars. 9 of thirteen rows have a value. Week two used a different set, so this is not a like-for-like comparison.

slides.title: W3-R032: same route, one facet falls below the cut
slides.label: Failure analysis / retrieval
slides.speaker: Doruk
slides.notes: Now the same journey with a case that fails, W3-R032. The resident asks two things: what a park fair needs for permission, and how to report a blocked entrance. After fusion, the access facet sits at 3 and the permit facet at 6. The reranker lifts YV-D021#limits from 17 to 5, and the permit facet slips to 7. The top-five cut leaves it out; without the reranker it sat at 6, still outside. Hit at five calls this a success; all facets at five does not.

slides.title: Five passages in, a fixed refusal out
slides.label: Failure analysis / retrieval
slides.speaker: Tarık
slides.notes: I am Tarık. The model received these five passages: the access facet at rank 3, but not the permit facet. It returned the fixed refusal, which our validator accepts as the fixed fallback, so it adds no claims to the claim rate. We record the root cause as retrieval: 1/2 required facets reached the context, and the missing one ranked 7.

slides.title: Every failure is assigned to one stage
slides.label: Failure analysis / W3.8
slides.speaker: Tarık
slides.notes: We assign every failure to the first stage where it went wrong. Retrieval: W3-R032. Generation: W3-R017, W3-U004. Provider: W3-R019, W3-R027. Judge: W3-R020. The cards show what each record is. Each stage points to a different fix.

slides.title: Judge vs human on 20 claims: 17 agree
slides.label: Failure analysis / evaluation
slides.speaker: Tarık
slides.notes: Can we trust the judge? The team labelled 20 claims by hand. Each dot is one claim, placed by human label and judge label. 17 fall on the diagonal; Cohen’s kappa is 0.771. All 3 disagreements are claims a human marked insufficient. These are historical claims with the earlier evidence, so this calibrates the rubric, not accuracy on today’s answers.

slides.title: The rules and reviews behind the numbers
slides.label: Failure analysis / evaluation
slides.speaker: Tarık
slides.notes: Two boundaries behind these numbers. The judge now accepts a contact detail only if an authorized source contains it. The team approved 31 of 31 documents and 38 of 38 test cases, recorded after the run on the same content. Our 2 customer interviews are done.

slides.title: Next week: three priorities, each tied to a metric
slides.label: Next week / plan
slides.speaker: Tarık
slides.notes: These are plans, not results; each names the metric it should move. First: clean rerun of retrieval and answers on the approved files at the tagged commit, for hit at 5, mrr, unsupported claims. Second: controlled lookup tool and sandbox writes with confirmation, for validated tool-result rate. Third: multi-step tasks with traces and limits, for task success. On the route, the new stations are tools, confirmation and an agent loop, and every station gets measured before we trust it.

slides.title: Every number traces back to a command and a hash
slides.label: Next week / reproducibility
slides.speaker: Tarık
slides.notes: Every number in this deck is read from recorded result files when the deck is built, so a corrected metric updates every slide. Retrieval runs locally without an API key, and corpus, index and question hashes travel with the results.

slides.title: Four questions we expect
slides.label: Questions and feedback
slides.speaker: Tarık
slides.notes: Thank you. We are ready for your questions. Each of these four cards opens a prepared answer with the evidence behind it, so pick any of them.
